title: Pivmecillinam

indications.title: Lower UTI Men aged 16 years and over (i.e. no fever, rigors or flank pain)
notes: Linked prescribing pathway: lower-uti-men-16-and-over — 2nd choice empiric treatment (whilst waiting sensitivities as per MSU) Trimethoprim resistance likely and nitrofurantoin unsuitable

interactions.description: Pivmecillinam potentially alters the anticoagulant effect of Acenocoumarol. Manufacturer advises monitor INR and adjust dose.
Pivmecillinam is predicted to increase the risk of toxicity when given with Methotrexate. Manufacturer advises monitor.
Pivmecillinam is predicted to increase the risk of bleeding events when given with Phenindione. Manufacturer makes no recommendation.
Valproate increases the risk of adverse effects when given with Pivmecillinam. Manufacturer advises avoid.
Pivmecillinam potentially alters the anticoagulant effect of Warfarin. Manufacturer advises monitor INR and adjust dose.

effects: Diarrhoea; hypersensitivity; nausea; skin reactions; thrombocytopenia; vomiting
Clostridioides difficile colitis; dizziness; fatigue; gastrointestinal discomfort; gastrointestinal disorders; headache; oral ulceration; vertigo
Agranulocytosis; angioedema; haemolytic anaemia; hepatic disorders; nephritis tubulointerstitial; neutropenia; pseudomembranous enterocolitis; seizure; severe cutaneous adverse reactions (SCARs)

pregnancyBreastfeeding: Not known to be harmful, but manufacturer advises avoid.
Trace amount in milk, but appropriate to use.
practicalPoints: Liver and renal function tests required in long-term use.
Manufacturer advises tablets should be swallowed whole with plenty of fluid during meals while sitting or standing.
Patient counselling is advised on administration of pivmecillinam hydrochloride tablets (posture).
